workflowInfo.workflowDescription: Point-in-time z/OS health snapshot: filesystems, ports, RACF, JES queue

variable.name: FS_WARN_PCT
variable.label: Filesystem Warning Threshold (%)
variable.abstract: Flag any mounted zFS above this usage percentage (default 80)
variable.description: Any filesystem whose used percentage meets or exceeds this value will be flagged WARN in the checkLargeMounts step. Expressed as an integer, e.g. 80 for 80%.

variable.name: RACF_GROUPS
variable.label: RACF Groups to Check
variable.abstract: Space-separated list of RACF group names to verify exist
variable.description: The checkRacfGroups step runs LISTGRP for each group name in this list. Separate names with a single space. Example: ZWEADMIN ZWESIGRP SYS1

variable.name: HEALTH_STATUS
variable.label: Overall Health Status
variable.abstract: Set by the operator after reviewing all checks: HEALTHY, DEGRADED, or CRITICAL
variable.description: Overall health verdict entered by the operator in the deriveHealth step after reviewing all automated outputs. Recorded in the final report.

variable.name: REPORT_PATH
variable.label: Report Output Path
variable.abstract: USS path where the health dashboard report will be written
variable.description: The full USS file path for the health dashboard report output.

step.name: checkZosmf
step.title: Check z/OSMF Connectivity
step.description: Sends GET /zosmf/info to confirm z/OSMF is reachable and records the system name and version. Prerequisite for all subsequent steps.
step.instructions:
Sends GET /zosmf/info. HTTP 200 confirms z/OSMF is reachable. The system name and z/OSMF version appear in the step output and are recorded in the final report.
PASS : HTTP 200 FAIL : Any other status

step.name: checkFilesystems
step.title: Check Filesystem Usage
step.description: Runs df -k to list all mounted filesystems with their total, used, and available space. Produces a summary table sorted by usage percentage.
step.instructions:
Runs df -k and formats a usage table for all mounted filesystems. Output is sorted by used percentage descending so the fullest filesystems appear first.
Review for any filesystems approaching capacity before the checkLargeMounts threshold check.

template.inlineTemplate: #!/bin/sh echo "=== Filesystem Usage ===" echo "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" echo "------------------------" printf "%-45s %10s %10s %10s %6s\n" "MOUNT POINT" "TOTAL(KB)" "USED(KB)" "AVAIL(KB)" "USE%" echo "-----------------------------------------------------------------------" df -k 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | while read LINE; do MOUNT=$(echo "$LINE" | awk '{print $1}') TOTAL=$(echo "$LINE" | awk '{print $2}') AVAIL=$(echo "$LINE" | awk '{print $3}') if [ -n "$TOTAL" ] && [ "$TOTAL" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then USED=$((TOTAL - AVAIL)) PCT=$(echo "$USED $TOTAL" | awk '{printf "%d", ($1/$2)*100}') printf "%-45s %10s %10s %10s %5s%%\n" "$MOUNT" "$TOTAL" "$USED" "$AVAIL" "$PCT" fi done echo "-----------------------------------------------------------------------" TOTAL_FS=$(df -k 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | wc -l | tr -d ' ') echo "Total mounted filesystems: $TOTAL_FS"

step.name: checkLargeMounts
step.title: Flag Filesystems Above Threshold
step.description: Scans all mounted filesystems and flags any above FS_WARN_PCT percent full. PASS if none exceed the threshold, WARN otherwise.
step.instructions:
Flags any filesystem at or above ${instance-FS_WARN_PCT}% usage as a warning.
PASS : All filesystems below the threshold WARN : One or more filesystems at or above threshold
Investigate any flagged filesystems before they fill completely — a full zFS will crash the address spaces using it.

template.inlineTemplate: #!/bin/sh THRESHOLD=${instance-FS_WARN_PCT} echo "=== Filesystem Threshold Check ===" echo "Warn threshold : ${THRESHOLD}%" echo "----------------------------------" WARN_COUNT=0 df -k 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | while read LINE; do MOUNT=$(echo "$LINE" | awk '{print $1}') TOTAL=$(echo "$LINE" | awk '{print $2}') AVAIL=$(echo "$LINE" | awk '{print $3}') if [ -n "$TOTAL" ] && [ "$TOTAL" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then USED=$((TOTAL - AVAIL)) PCT=$(echo "$USED $TOTAL" | awk '{printf "%d", ($1/$2)*100}') if [ "$PCT" -ge "$THRESHOLD" ] 2>/dev/null; then FREE_GB=$(echo "$AVAIL 1048576" | awk '{printf "%.2f", $1/$2}') echo "WARN: $MOUNT is ${PCT}% full (${FREE_GB} GB free)" WARN_COUNT=$((WARN_COUNT+1)) fi fi done echo "----------------------------------" if [ $WARN_COUNT -eq 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "RESULT : PASS (no filesystems above ${THRESHOLD}%)" else echo "RESULT : WARN ($WARN_COUNT filesystem(s) at or above ${THRESHOLD}%)" fi

step.name: checkActivePorts
step.title: Check Active Listening Ports
step.description: Runs netstat to count and list all ports currently in LISTEN state. Provides a snapshot of active services on the system.
step.instructions:
Runs netstat -an and filters for LISTEN entries. Reports a count of listening ports and lists the first 30 for review.
Use this output to spot unexpected services or confirm expected services (Zowe, z/OSMF, etc.) are listening.

template.inlineTemplate: #!/bin/sh echo "=== Active Listening Ports ===" echo "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" echo "------------------------------" LISTEN_OUT=$(netstat -an 2>/dev/null | grep -i "listen") COUNT=$(echo "$LISTEN_OUT" | grep -c "." 2>/dev/null) echo "Total ports in LISTEN state: $COUNT" echo "" echo "--- Port list (first 40) ---" echo "$LISTEN_OUT" | head -40 echo "----------------------------" echo "" echo "--- Key service ports ---" for PORT in 443 7554 7556 7552 7553 8544 10443; do HIT=$(echo "$LISTEN_OUT" | grep "\\.$PORT ") if [ -n "$HIT" ]; then echo "PORT $PORT : LISTENING" else echo "PORT $PORT : not found" fi done echo "RESULT : PASS ($COUNT ports listening)"

step.name: checkRacfGroups
step.title: Check Key RACF Groups
step.description: Runs LISTGRP for each group in RACF_GROUPS to confirm they exist and have members. Missing groups indicate incomplete security configuration.

template.inlineTemplate: #!/bin/sh GROUPS="${instance-RACF_GROUPS}" echo "=== RACF Group Check ===" echo "Groups : $GROUPS" echo "------------------------" PASS=0 FAIL=0 for GRP in $GROUPS; do OUT=$(tsocmd "LISTGRP $GRP" 2>&1) RC=$? echo "--- LISTGRP $GRP (RC=$RC) ---" echo "$OUT" | head -10 if [ $RC -eq 0 ]; then echo "STATUS : $GRP EXISTS" PASS=$((PASS+1)) else echo "STATUS : $GRP NOT FOUND" FAIL=$((FAIL+1)) fi echo "" done echo "------------------------" if [ $FAIL -eq 0 ]; then echo "RESULT : PASS ($PASS group(s) verified)" else echo "RESULT : FAIL ($FAIL group(s) missing, $PASS found)" fi

step.name: checkJesQueue
step.title: Check JES Queue Snapshot
step.description: Issues tsocmd STATUS to capture a snapshot of jobs currently active, waiting, or held in the JES queue. Surfaces job backlog at the time of the health check.
step.instructions:
Issues tsocmd STATUS to list all jobs in the JES queue visible to the ANDRE user ID.
Reports: - Total jobs found - Jobs in execution (ACTIVE) - Jobs waiting (INPUT/CONVERT) - Jobs held (HELD)
A large queue backlog or many held jobs may indicate a system performance or configuration issue.

template.inlineTemplate: #!/bin/sh echo "=== JES Queue Snapshot ===" echo "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" echo "--------------------------" OUT=$(tsocmd "STATUS" 2>&1) echo "$OUT" echo "--------------------------" TOTAL=$(echo "$OUT" | grep -c "JOB\|STC\|TSU" 2>/dev/null) ACTIVE=$(echo "$OUT" | grep -c "EXECUTING\|ACTIVE" 2>/dev/null) HELD=$(echo "$OUT" | grep -ic "held" 2>/dev/null) echo "Jobs visible : $TOTAL" echo "Executing : $ACTIVE" echo "Held : $HELD" echo "RESULT : PASS (JES queue snapshot captured)"

step.name: deriveHealth
step.title: Record Health Verdict
step.description: Operator reviews all automated check outputs and records the overall system health status in HEALTH_STATUS.
step.instructions:
Review the spool output from all preceding steps and set HEALTH_STATUS to one of:
HEALTHY — all checks passed, system operating normally DEGRADED — warnings found, system functional but needs attention CRITICAL — one or more failures, immediate action required
Consider the following when setting the verdict: - Any filesystems above the warning threshold? - Any expected ports not listening? - Any RACF groups missing? - Unusual JES queue depth or held jobs?

step.name: writeReport
step.title: Write Health Dashboard Report
step.description: Writes a timestamped health dashboard report to REPORT_PATH on USS and surfaces it on the JES spool for archiving or forwarding.

template.inlineTemplate: #!/bin/sh REPORT="${instance-REPORT_PATH}" TS=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') echo "Writing health report to $REPORT" echo "============================================================" > "$REPORT" echo " z/OS Health Dashboard Report" >> "$REPORT" echo " Generated : $TS" >> "$REPORT" echo "============================================================" >> "$REPORT" echo "" >> "$REPORT" echo "CONFIGURATION" >> "$REPORT" echo " FS warn threshold : ${instance-FS_WARN_PCT}%" >> "$REPORT" echo " RACF groups : ${instance-RACF_GROUPS}" >> "$REPORT" echo "" >> "$REPORT" echo "CHECKS PERFORMED" >> "$REPORT" echo " 1. z/OSMF connectivity - see checkZosmf step" >> "$REPORT" echo " 2. Filesystem usage table - see checkFilesystems step" >> "$REPORT" echo " 3. Filesystem thresholds - see checkLargeMounts step" >> "$REPORT" echo " 4. Active listening ports - see checkActivePorts step" >> "$REPORT" echo " 5. RACF group existence - see checkRacfGroups step" >> "$REPORT" echo " 6. JES queue snapshot - see checkJesQueue step" >> "$REPORT" echo "" >> "$REPORT" echo "HEALTH VERDICT" >> "$REPORT" echo " ${instance-HEALTH_STATUS}" >> "$REPORT" echo "" >> "$REPORT" echo " Recorded at : $TS" >> "$REPORT" echo " Workflow : zos-health-dashboard v1.0" >> "$REPORT" echo "" >> "$REPORT" echo "============================================================" >> "$REPORT" echo "" echo "=== Report written to $REPORT ===" cat "$REPORT"
